plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE with power caveat
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12,000 genes x 6 samples plus a gene-symbol column; /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv) from Salmon quantification of human liver, with a 6 x 2 metadata table giving one condition per sample: 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two halves — which genes differ, and how much confidence three replicates per group buys — so the plan answers both explicitly rather than producing a gene table alone.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any test: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes. With n=3 per group a single aberrant sample can drive the whole result, so the QC exists to detect that before it is silently absorbed into the model. T1S2 does the modelling: minimal pre-filter (>= 10 counts in >= 3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2 (no pre-normalisation), design ~condition with control set explicitly as the reference level so a positive log2FC means higher in treated, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Counts are gene-level and already summarised, so tximport length offsets are not available here; the step must state that the length-offset route was not possible and that a fold change driven purely by isoform-length shift cannot be excluded. DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers as NA at n=3 rather than replacing them, and those NAs must be reported separately from independent-filtering NAs.

T1S3 is the confidence half of the question and is not decorative: an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design, reported as the overlap with DESeq2 (intersection = high-confidence set, method-unique genes listed separately, never the union), plus an explicit power statement at 3 replicates per group. Published benchmarks at n=3 recover only a minority of true DE genes, concentrated at large fold changes, so absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes (ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed choice is stated and taken deliberately, because it scales effect by uncertainty and does not tie at saturated p-values) into fgsea against human MSigDB hallmark sets, with human Reactome as the second collection. The ranked method is the right one here precisely because n=3 will likely yield few individually significant genes, and an over-representation test on a short list has no power. T1S4 assembles the reproducible report.

No drug-target, biomarker or safety step is planned: the condition column names a treatment but the profile carries no compound identity, no exposure data and no outcome labels, so any druggability or safety claim would be speculation rather than analysis.

edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
Reproducible report with power statement, MA and dispersion plots, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, method overlap, leading edge genes

steps.name: Reproducible DE and enrichment report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control liver, and how much should we believe it' given 3 replicates per group?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Lead with the power statement at 3 replicates per group, before any gene table. Then give: the method and every package version, the design formula and the contrast written as (condition, treated, control), the thresholds used, the number of genes tested after filtering and the number differentially expressed; the MA plot and the dispersion plot as fit diagnostics; the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value with the shrinkage estimator named in the header; the DESeq2/edgeR overlap with the intersection as the high-confidence set; the enrichment results with collection names and versions, ranking metric, universe, size window, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set with leading-edge overlaps marked; and a statement that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, the random seed used for the fgsea permutations, and the gene-set collection versions. State plainly what the data cannot support — no compound identity, exposure, or outcome data is present, so no druggability, biomarker, or safety inference is made.
steps.context: The two halves of the research question are answered here jointly: the gene list, and the confidence qualification that a 3-vs-3 design forces on it. Overclaiming at this sample size is the main failure mode this step exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: The power statement at 3 replicates per group appears before the gene tables
Method, package versions, design formula, contrast direction, thresholds, n tested and n DE genes all reported
MA plot and dispersion plot included as fit diagnostics
Gene table carries unshrunken LFC, shrunken (apeglm) LFC and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap reported with the intersection named as the high-confidence set
Enrichment section reports collection and version, ranking metric, universe, size window, and per-set leading-edge genes
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, random seed and collection versions is stored with the results
An explicit statement that absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change at this replicate number
An explicit statement that no drug-target, biomarker or safety inference is drawn, because the inputs carry no compound, exposure or outcome data
constraints: Do not rank the gene table by the unshrunken log2 fold change
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Report a null or near-null DE result plainly if that is the outcome; do not relax thresholds to produce a list
Do not speculate about mechanism of action, drug targets, or clinical relevance
caveats: A short or empty significant gene list is a real and reportable outcome for a 3-vs-3 design and must not be presented as an analysis failure
Enrichment hits at this power are hypotheses for follow-up, not established biology
